overview.title: Where Roman Sala meets Islamic Rabat
overview.p1: Chellah encloses the ruins of Roman Sala and a Merinid necropolis within fortified walls. Paths wind past broken columns, a minaret stub, pools and gardens. Storks nest on the walls in season, adding to the atmosphere. It is one of the most peaceful major sites in the capital.
overview.p2: Wear good shoes; surfaces are uneven. Combine with Hassan in the morning or late afternoon light for photos.

food.title: Eating near Chellah
food.p1: Limited options at the gate. Eat in Hassan, Agdal or the medina before or after.
food.p2: Treat Chellah as a monument stop, not a restaurant cluster.
food.li2: Café near the entrance if open.
food.li3: Lunch in Agdal or Hassan after.
food.li5: Dinner back in the medina or centre.

q1.question: Is Chellah worth it?
q1.answer: Yes for history fans and anyone wanting a green, quiet contrast to the centre.

q2.question: Storks year-round?
q2.answer: Nesting is seasonal; walls still impress without them.

q3.question: How far from Hassan Tower?
q3.answer: Short taxi ride or a longer walk.

q4.question: Guided tour useful?
q4.answer: Optional — panels help, guides add depth.

q5.question: Good with children?
q5.answer: Yes if they like open-air ruins; watch steps.
